**The two readings agreeing at 3/3 is itself the finding.** Unlike its `service-knowledge` sibling — where the split contradicted the ledger — this package carried no config-tier pile at all, so the 3 were genuinely code-tier from the start. Reporting the agreement is as informative as reporting a divergence would have been, and the card required both numbers precisely so this case is distinguishable from the other.

**The fix uses an accessor that already existed.** The three sites dot-read the private `AutomationEngine#flows`; they now call `await engine.getFlow(name)`. I checked that `getFlow` is pre-existing on `origin/main` rather than introduced here — it is, and it is already the idiom in `config-unknown-keys.test.ts`, `canonicalize-stored-flow.test.ts` and `engine.test.ts`. No widened source signature, no cast, no bracket-notation workaround. Note the deleted DEBT entry framed this as an open question (*"whether tests may read private state at all"*); using the public accessor answers it in the direction that does not weaken the class.

`paths` was measured and rejected at 0 → **648** errors (647 TS6059 + 1 TS6133), every TS6059 billed to another package's source and **zero** in this package's own `src/`.

## ⚠️ Landing is serialized, and that is this seat's doing

All three sibling PRs — #15147 (#15049), #15152 (#15048), and #15050's when it arrives — touch **the same three files**:

- `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`
- `scripts/check-type-source-resolution.mjs`
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`

Measured across the three branches, not assumed. They will conflict textually: each deletes a different DEBT entry and adds a different registry entry in the same regions of the same two files.

⇒ **They land one at a time, not concurrently.** #15147 goes first (it is furthest along and its ACCEPT is already posted). When it merges, this PR needs `origin/main` merged in and the two gate files re-resolved before it is armed — and the resolution is "keep both entries", since the changes are additive in different rows. That work belongs to this card's dev in its own worktree; ⛔ this seat does not write it.

This is a dispatch consequence, not a defect in anyone's PR: three same-family cards were launched in parallel, which is good for throughput and bad for a shared ledger file. The correct trade is still parallel authoring plus serialized landing — recorded here so the next same-family batch is sequenced deliberately rather than rediscovering it.

⛔ Not arming this PR yet, for that reason and not because anything is wrong with it.

Both present ⇒ the "keep every entry" resolution held; neither sibling's graduation was clobbered. `8aff199c` is a **real merge commit**, ⛔ not a rebase, so anyone holding this branch keeps a valid checkout. `pnpm-lock.yaml` was regenerated with the repo's tooling (`pnpm install` left it byte-unchanged, `--frozen-lockfile` exits 0) ⛔ rather than hand-merged. The DEBT summary line is **computed at runtime** (`${Object.keys(DEBT).length}`, `${debtTotal}`), so it cannot carry a stale hardcoded total — verified in the source, which is why only the `check-type-source-resolution.mjs` entry needed its prose recomputed.

### Two things this round did that are worth keeping

1. **The dev asked instead of widening.** Its instruction was an explicit list plus "⛔ nothing else"; it found a *seventh* stale sentence of the same defect class (the `Declined` line claiming `service-knowledge` still lacks a `typecheck` script — false since `8422acd`) and **stopped at the fence to ask**. That is the correct reading of a boundary: quietly widening is how a reviewed diff stops matching what was reviewed. Authorised, and it changed that one sentence only.

2. ⭐ **It then applied the lesson to itself.** Told that my enumeration had been incomplete, it re-swept the whole body **by predicate rather than by memory** and reported every candidate with a verdict — including two it correctly left alone as *not falsified* (`2cc4610304` and the `9 deps / 648 / 647` breakdown, both still true post-merge) and one it flagged as **"judged not falsified, ⛔ not re-measured"** (`555 files` / `103`). ⚠️ **That last distinction is the valuable one** — "I checked and it still holds" and "nothing could have changed it" are different claims, and collapsing them is how a stale figure survives a review. Keeping them apart, and keeping the weaker one out of the PR body, is exactly right.

**My failure, recorded:** the enumeration was mine and it was incomplete — the **second** time this round (on #15072 the dev listed two stale `packages/spec` sentences and a fresh grep found a third, `:110`). Same shape both times: enumerating from memory of what one wrote instead of searching for the **predicate that went false**. Carried to the seat post.

The `Gates` section still reads *"Three commands (`check:pm-dispatch-gates`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:slot-lookup`) needed longer than a 90s probe budget…"*. The dev flagged it and asked. **Leave it.** It is a true historical statement about the pre-merge round's *methodology*, not a measurement that the merge falsified, and the newly added scoping sentence already binds this section's **figures** to the post-merge re-run at `c6d25b73`. Correcting it would be tidying, not accuracy — and ⛔ churn on a reviewed body is not free.
